clue.text: A romance where nothing's right

parts.note: nothing is love in tennis scoring, and the 's (is) adds an S
the right wing in politics is the Tory side

explanation.surface: A love affair in which nothing goes as it should.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'nothing's' is read as 'nothing is', so LOVE plus the S of the 's. TORY means a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale of courtship and passion is a romance in the literary sense.

clue.text: Drove madly round to get exhausted

indicators.note: madly says the letters of drove are thrown about wildly into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone drove recklessly in circles until they were worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges the clue's first word; 'exhausted' looks like an adjective but goes with 'get' as a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwork or overexert yourself is to tire yourself out, a dictionary sense.

clue.text: The egghead joins up, gaining respect

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to join someone is to meet them, so joins gives meets

explanation.surface: An intellectual signs up and wins admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the synonym for 'joins' in this down entry; 'egghead' gives only the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard, a straight synonym for respect.

clue.text: Cheats playing pontoon?

definitions.meaning: in pontoon a player who asks for another card face up says twist

explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for the card game blackjack; the question mark flags the second, game-specific sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindles and frauds are twists in slang, while card players call for a card with the same word.

clue.text: Having finished work, went to bed

definitions.meaning: someone who has stopped working for good is pensioned off
to turn in for the night is a formal sense of the verb

explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner has left employment, and a sleeper heading upstairs has also withdrawn for the night.

clue.text: Probing into a variety of pies over a period

indicators.note: a variety of signals a mixture, so the letters of pies are rearranged

parts.note: over in the sense of concerning or about gives on
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone pokes about among a range of pastries for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges the pastry word; 'over' as 'on' means concerning, as in a talk on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is covert probing for secrets, so the noun matches probing used as a noun.

clue.text: Terrifying experience of the dark horse

parts.note: the dark hours are the night
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A frightening encounter with a mysterious horse in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream or any ordeal of dread is a terrifying experience.

clue.text: Callous fellow, quite plain-speaking

parts.note: a fellow is a male, referred to as he
someone wholly artless is guileless and frank in speech

explanation.surface: An unfeeling man who speaks with blunt candour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking pity or warmth, as in a cold-blooded or unfeeling person.

clue.text: Hope is a feature of the church

definitions.meaning: to hope for something is to aim for it, as a verb
a church often has a tall pointed steeple, read as A plus that word

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as A SPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim or yearn is to hope, and a pointed steeple tops many a church.

clue.text: Tiny trace may lead to conviction

indicators.note: may lead to says these letters can be turned into something else, here rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny scrap of evidence might secure a guilty verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' looks legal in the surface but here means firm belief; the letters of TINY TRACE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute sureness of belief is conviction in its non-legal sense.

clue.text: Decline with little hesitation

parts.note: taken as written
er is the short sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an offer after barely pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade, shrivel or weaken is to decline.

clue.text: To die will be an awfully big Barrie (Peter Pan)

definitions.text: To die will be an awfully big Barrie (Peter Pan)

parts.words: To die will be an awfully big Barrie (Peter Pan)
parts.note: a famous line spoken by Peter Pan in J M Barrie's play, with its last word missing, to be supplied

explanation.walkthrough: Peter Pan says 'To die will be an awfully big ...' in Barrie's play; the bracketed attribution tells you to finish the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan treats death as one more exciting escapade, the missing word of his line.

clue.text: Gloss over

parts.note: read not as to hide a fault but literally as to coat something with a glossy finish

explanation.definitionFit: A hard shiny coating applied on top of metal, pottery or teeth is glossy paint or glaze.

clue.text: Greatness unfortunately makes enemies

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of greatness are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fame sadly alienates people.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone or set people apart is to turn them into foes.

clue.text: Check about a writer's hoard

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to check is to stop or halt, which is to stay
George Bernard Shaw is the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Inspecting a novelist's secret stockpile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the verb meaning halt around the article and playwright; the 's reads as 'is', linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To put by in a secret store is to hoard, as a verb.

clue.text: Hungered possibly, receiving nothing, and got more harsh

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so a letter is placed inside
possibly says the letters of hungered may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone hungry, given nothing to eat, became coarser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HUNGERED to RUGHENED, and 'receiving' puts O inside after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or become coarser and rougher is to grow more harsh.

clue.text: Tot worrying dad

indicators.note: worrying means pulling about or harassing, so the letters of dad are disturbed

explanation.surface: A toddler pestering their father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child; it is the verb, as in tot up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up a column of figures is to sum them.

clue.text: A very short distance behind

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot, a short unit of length

explanation.surface: Just a tiny bit back.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical word for towards the stern or rear.

clue.text: Boring prohibitionist

definitions.meaning: dull and uninteresting, as a dull speech is
a person who supports banning alcohol

explanation.definitionFit: A tedious talk is dull, and a teetotal campaigner wants the country without alcohol.

clue.text: Blows up and so shows to advantage

definitions.meaning: to detonate a bomb or explosive charge
a frame or colour that enhances something by contrast

explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a charge, or to enhance by contrast as a frame does a picture, are both senses of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Notices conveying compliments

definitions.meaning: observes or looks at, a verb
good wishes, as at the end of a letter

explanation.definitionFit: To look at attentively, and the kind wishes sent at a letter's close, share the word.

clue.text: Some of the gentry are very irritating

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Certain members of the upper class are a real nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that tax your patience annoy you, as in 'they test my patience'.

clue.text: Person facing facts about a certain leaning

parts.note: re is Latin for about, as in business letters
a list is a tilt or lean, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone confronting the truth about their particular bias.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist who deals with things as they are faces reality.

clue.text: Singer suffering a breakdown getting leave

indicators.note: suffering a breakdown suggests falling apart, so the letters of singer are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist with a nervous collapse quits.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a job is to step down from it.

clue.text: A little fiend in general, that's the conclusion

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A minor devil in general marks the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The close or finish of a story is its end, so the conclusion.

clue.text: Greek character without a casual shirt? Shame!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a tee, or T-shirt, is a casual shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: A Greek man without a T-shirt: how embarrassing!
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: SIGMA goes around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of disgrace attached to someone is a stain of shame.

clue.text: Advocates entering burning city

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: something burning is hot
the Bar is the collective body of barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers go into a town on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: HOBART is the capital of Tasmania, Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian capital is an Australian city.

clue.text: Offering transport to people is a bloomer!

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Giving a vehicle to the public is a blunder!
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink or clove-scented garden flower is something that blooms.

clue.text: Approached tight newsman

parts.note: tight with money means mean, stingy, near
ed is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A stingy journalist drew close.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw close is to approach.

clue.text: Where rail-travellers find the fare

parts.note: fare reads as ticket money, but here it is food served on board

explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant carriage on a train is where passengers eat.

clue.text: The guy avoiding a woman turned colour

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name

indicators.note: turned says the colour word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A man ducking a woman who has gone red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reads the colour backwards; 'The guy avoiding' is the definition, not a man in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dodging or escaping is a dodger.

clue.text: All men do!

parts.note: do is a noun, a party, and this one is for men only, before a wedding

explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor celebration attended only by men is an all-male do.
